Question 2 · your D1660

A browser that will not store anything

Some browsers refuse to store anything for a website, for example a browser set to block all website data. The app still opens there and works, but it holds your work only until the page is reloaded or closed. Today nothing says so. The Tracker's corner shows "● saved" in green, and the top bar shows no warning. A reload then loses the work, on every page, not only the Tracker.

Reproduced on the app: with the browser's storage blocked, Student A was given a grade on ST-02. The corner said "● saved". After a reload the grade was gone, and the corner still said "● saved". The result was the same on a desktop and on a phone.

Today

RecommendedA · A band under the top bar, on every page

The band takes the look of your "Not saved" strip (D1655): the drawn warning sign, a bold lead, quieter words after it. It has no Retry, because there is nothing to retry. The page moves down one band height (36 px), so nothing is covered. While the band is up, the Tracker's corner shows nothing.

Not keptthis browser loses your work on a reload

It fits on your iPhone's width in one line. It needs 304 px of the band's 374 px, and 347 px even in wider letters. Longer wordings, such as "This browser will not keep your work · a reload loses it", were cut off in the wider letters, so they were dropped.

What a person sees: on every page, a plain warning that a reload will lose their work, and nobody is told "saved" when the work is not kept. Cost: one new band for the whole app, a small job.

B · Only the Tracker's corner changes

The corner turns amber, the colour of its "Saving…", and says the work is not kept. On a desktop, resting the mouse on it shows the full sentence, "This browser will not keep your work: a reload loses it".

● not kept

Only these words fit the phone's corner, using 65 of its 72 px. A longer wording such as "● kept until a reload" fits a desktop but is cut off on a phone.

What a person sees: the Tracker stops saying "saved", but Edit Schedule and every other page still lose the work without a word. Cost: the smallest job.

C · Leave it until the database step

What a person sees: what the "Today" pictures above show. Until the database step, a person in such a browser keeps losing work without a word, and the Tracker tells them it is saved. Cost: nothing built now.

Recommended: A. The app should never tell a person "saved" when the work is not kept. A gives one warning that looks the same on every page, in the look of your "Not saved" strip (D1655), with its own words, so "Not saved" keeps meaning a save that failed.
